whatItIs: A position-independent executable stored under jniLibs with a .so name. PackageManager treats any lib/<abi>/*.so entry as a native library, extracts it to nativeLibraryDir, and marks it 0755, which is what lets the app run it with ProcessBuilder. The helper is exec'd, never loaded as a library; it is the exploit payload passed to it as argv[2] that gets dlopen'd.

build.note: The rule above is the payloads repository Makefile ROOT_HELPER rule verbatim. The helper includes no local or target headers, so the build takes no target context. tools/helper-marker-removal.patch is then applied and the result is a different source from upstream; see localChanges. Reproduce with tools/build-helper.sh, which pins the commit, applies the patch, and verifies every hash below.

replaces.builtFrom: an older payloads revision (79f42b0-era su_daemon.c), not from main

behaviourChanges: late-load now first attempts `logcat late-load --ephemeral --package-name me.weishu.kernelsu`, then checks the KernelSU control interface, and retries once without --ephemeral if the module is not live. The retry exists because the Samsung-patched KernelSU 3.2.5 loader rejects --ephemeral with a usage error yet still exits 0, so the exit status alone cannot gate the fallback. The bundled loader contains no `ephemeral` string at all, so on a clean device the first attempt is expected to be rejected and the retry to do the work.
The bootstrap readiness marker present in the pinned upstream source is removed here; see localChanges.
unchangedContracts: /data/local/tmp/ksud-s25u-kdp stays the compiled-in loader path; the app must stage the ksud under exactly that name.
/system/bin/logcat stays the bind-mount target used to exec the loader.
me.weishu.kernelsu stays the package name passed to the loader.
localChanges: tools/helper-marker-removal.patch removes the bootstrap readiness marker. Upstream's version reads a path from /data/local/tmp/cve43499-root-marker-path, a directory any shell can write to, and then opens that path as root with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and no ownership, mode, symlink or directory check. That is a root-write primitive with attacker-chosen destination, and this app never uses the feature, so it is removed rather than merely left dormant. The patch also restores umh_main's original three-argument check, since the fourth argument existed only to carry the marker path.
No other source line is changed. The --ephemeral attempt and its fallback, the loader path, the logcat bind-mount target and the package name are all byte-identical to the pinned upstream source.
requiresFreshP0Session: The upstream manifest sets requiresFreshP0Session true. The app does not implement it and the bundled payload does not enforce it: the e1q target header does not define APP_REQUIRE_FRESH_P0_SESSION, so the payload takes the branch that retains a discovered P0 offset and injects it into the next child. The payloads porting record documents EXPLOIT_ATTEMPTS=24 and a golden run on attempt 5/48, and contains no supervisor-retained diagnostic, so it does not establish that the retention branch was exercised. The app keeps the upstream behaviour rather than changing tested exploit semantics on the strength of a field nothing reads.
